ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: The changing trends of the net photosynthetic rates of plants A and B with light intensity are shown in the figure. Answer the following question: When plants A and B are planted separately, if the planting density is too high, which plant has the larger decrease in net photosynthetic rate?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, the horizontal axis represents light intensity, and the vertical axis represents net photosynthetic rate. Curve A is a solid line; it rises obviously as light intensity increases and finally reaches a relatively high net photosynthetic rate. Curve B is a dashed line; it rises more slowly as light intensity increases, is overall relatively gentle, and its final net photosynthetic rate is lower than that of A. Then reason: When planted separately, if the planting density is too high, the plants will shade one another, causing the light intensity received by a single plant to decrease. Comparing the magnitude of change of the two curves when light intensity decreases, curve A is steeper, is more sensitive to changes in light intensity, and has a larger decrease in net photosynthetic rate; curve B is gentler and has a smaller decrease. Therefore, the plant with the larger decrease in net photosynthetic rate is A.
